title: Graphic design basics
examples: How do I make my design look professional?
What is the difference between contrast and similarity in design?
Can you show me how to use different fonts together?

explain.say: Today we are learning about the basic rules of graphic design.

items: Repetition: using things over and over

draw.text: Design Principles: Contrast, Alignment, Repetition, Proximity

explain.say: Contrast means making things stand out from each other clearly.
Alignment means lining up elements so they look organized and straight.
Repetition means using the same element multiple times for consistency.

items: Step 3: Use a third blue square

explain.say: Proximity means keeping things that belong together close to each other.
Now let us look at fonts, which is also very important for design.

faq.q: What is the most important rule in graphic design?
faq.a: There is no single most important rule, but good design uses all these principles together effectively. It is about making it easy for the viewer to understand.
asks: What should I focus on first?
Which principle is the most crucial one?

faq.q: How do I know if my alignment is correct?
faq.a: Try drawing faint vertical or horizontal lines behind your text to see if everything lines up perfectly. Consistent straight lines look professional.
asks: Is it okay to have some things slightly off?
What makes a layout look crooked?

faq.q: Can I use a lot of different fonts in one design?
faq.a: It is best to limit yourself to two or three complementary fonts maximum. Too many fonts will make the design look messy and confusing.
asks: How many fonts should I use?

faq.q: What is the difference between repetition and pattern?
faq.a: Repetition is using the same element multiple times for consistency. A pattern is a decorative, repeating visual design element.
asks: Is pattern a type of repetition?

faq.q: Does proximity only apply to text?
faq.a: No, proximity applies to any related items, like images, icons, or sections of information. Grouping related visuals helps the viewer process information.
asks: Can I group pictures using proximity?
What if I group things that are not related?

facts: Contrast can be shown through size, color, or weight.
Alignment creates a sense of order and professionalism in a layout.
Repetition helps build a consistent brand identity across materials.
Proximity guides the viewer's eye by suggesting relationships between elements.
Serif fonts have small decorative lines called serifs at the ends of strokes.

quiz.say: If you place a title far away from its main body text, which principle are you ignoring?
quiz.why: Proximity suggests that things placed close together are related to each other.

wrong.0: Alignment is about lining things up straight, which is a different rule.
wrong.1: Repetition means using the same thing over and over again.
wrong.3: Contrast is about making things look different, not about grouping them.

quiz.say: Which font style is generally considered more formal or traditional?
quiz.why: Serif fonts, with their little feet, are often associated with classic or formal documents.

wrong.1: Sans-serif fonts are usually seen as modern and clean, not formal.
wrong.2: Block is not a recognized font style principle.
wrong.3: Script fonts look like handwriting, which is a different category.

quiz.say: To make a headline jump out from the rest of the text, you should use:
quiz.why: Contrast is the best way to make one element visually pop against others.

wrong.1: Alignment only tells you how to line things up, not how to make them stand out.
wrong.2: Proximity only deals with grouping related items together.
wrong.3: Repetition keeps things consistent, which can make the headline blend in.
